newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industrialists see '97 trade gap at $11 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industrialists see '97 trade gap at $11 bln.

text.p: Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said the trade deficit for the whole of 1997 should reach $11 billion.
The CNI said imports would probably amount to $62 billion while exports should amount to $51 billion in 1997. The CNI made its forecast in its June foreign trade bulletin.

"Even though the trade deficit is likely to expand during the second half now that seasonal factors benefiting exports of primary goods have come to an end, other factors will prevent another major surge in imports," the CNI said.

These factors include a drop in consumer demand as a result of credit restrictions and greater household indebtedness, as well as restrictions on import financing, which have been implemented by the government and are starting to bite.

The CNI said imports would increase less rapidly in the second half of this year than in the second half of 1996, when imports jumped to an average $5 billion a month from an average $3.9 billion a month in the first half.
The recent re-introduction of an export credit guarantee system will also boost Brazilian exports and make them more competitive, the CNI said.
Brazil's trade deficit in 1996 was $5.5 billion, up from $3.2 billion the previous year, and a huge swing from a $10 billion surplus in 1994.
The government has refused to forecast the trade deficit for this year.

Market analysts on average expect an $11.4 billion trade gap for this year, according to the latest Reuter survey. That figure is somewhat lower than predictions at the start of 1997 for a trade gap of up to $15 billion. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
